title: Beeswax room-freshener disc
subtitle: A slow-release wax disc for cupboards and wardrobes
excerpt: Small beeswax discs scented with lavender and bergamot essential oils, poured into silicone moulds and hung or placed in drawers, wardrobes, and linen cupboards. Each disc releases a light scent for two to three months.
sourceNotes: Beeswax as a slow-release fragrance carrier: general candlemaking and aromatherapy literature. Essential oil loading in beeswax: standard formulation reference (3-5% for a non-combustion wax product). Bergamot and lavender pet-safety cautions: ASPCA toxic substances database.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles to 12 discs easily; keep essential oil percentage the same.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a batch and store in a sealed box; the discs keep two years before the scent fades.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps two years in a sealed box in a cool cupboard. The fragrance fades after two to three months of active use once unwrapped. Discard if the beeswax cracks or develops a rancid smell. The wax itself does not go off; the essential oil is the life-limiting component.

glossaryTerms.definition: The percentage of essential oil or fragrance oil added to melted wax. For non-combustion wax objects (discs, ornaments), a 3 to 5% loading by weight is standard. Too high a loading and the oil bleeds out of the wax surface.

content.text: Beeswax room-freshener discs are small cast wax shapes for drawers, wardrobes, and linen cupboards. Beeswax holds essential oils at 3 to 5% by weight and releases them slowly as the surface warms at room temperature. The
here is 4%, which gives a light but lasting scent. Each disc releases fragrance for about two to three months.
Lavender and bergamot essential oils are toxic to cats. Do not use in rooms cats have access to.

items.prepNote: cosmetic-grade beeswax pellets; forms 6 discs at approximately 25 g each including the EO
optional; lifts the lavender with a citrus top note

content.text: Place the beeswax pellets in the candle pouring pitcher. Set the pitcher in a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie) over low heat. Melt slowly. Do not leave over direct heat.
Cool and add the essential oils

Remove the pitcher from the heat when the beeswax is fully melted. Let it cool to 58 to 62°C. Beeswax solidifies at around 62°C; adding the essential oils below that temperature reduces evaporation but still allows the beeswax to remain pourable. Stir the essential oils in gently.

Pour slowly into the silicone moulds. Beeswax shrinks slightly as it sets; top up the moulds with a second pour if a slight well forms. Leave at room temperature for at least two hours before unmoulding.
Place a disc in a drawer, wardrobe, or linen cupboard. Or thread a ribbon through a small hole pressed in the disc before it sets, to hang. Replace when the fragrance fades.
Store unused discs in a sealed box in a cool, dark place. Two years shelf life. Each disc gives two to three months of active fragrance once unwrapped. The wax itself is stable indefinitely.
